decision: Use a deterministic local Node QA evidence runner as a fail-closed fallback while GitHub-hosted runners fail before their first workflow step.

context.githubHostedRunnerSymptom: Ubuntu and macOS preflight jobs fail with no workflow steps executed.
context.constraint: Do not weaken GitHub CI or production security controls; local evidence is supplemental until hosted CI returns.

independentReviews.preferred: mirror the five Node QA shards locally and bind evidence to a clean exact git SHA
independentReviews.reason: keeps test scope aligned with CI and prevents evidence from dirty or different source trees

independentReviews.preferred: fail closed on dirty worktree, SHA mismatch, timeout, spawn errors, or any shard failure
independentReviews.reason: avoids treating partial execution or unverifiable source state as readiness evidence

independentReviews.preferred: sequential shard execution with bounded timeouts and one JSON report
independentReviews.reason: predictable CPU/RAM footprint for a laptop/Qube and minimal new runtime surface

alternatives.rejectedBecause: leaves agents idle and provides no executable QA path during an external runner outage

alternatives.approach: replace GitHub CI with local QA
alternatives.rejectedBecause: would weaken independent hosted validation and could hide environment-specific regressions

alternatives.approach: add a self-hosted GitHub runner immediately
alternatives.rejectedBecause: adds persistent credentials, runner lifecycle, network exposure, and operational complexity before a simpler offline fallback is exhausted
reduces wall-clock latency but increases peak CPU/RAM and makes laptop/Qube fault diagnosis noisier

comparison.correctness: high: exact same Node shard membership plus clean-SHA binding
comparison.regressionRisk: low: QA-only code, no MissionQueue/coordinator mutation semantics changed
comparison.qa: unit tests cover all-pass, shard failure, dirty tree, SHA mismatch, and timeout

limitations: Does not provide native Swift/iOS compiler evidence on Linux/Qubes.
Report digest is integrity metadata, not a cryptographic signature or remote attestation.
REAL-WORKER readiness still requires real Qubes qualification evidence and restored independent CI.
next: Run npm run qa:local on the exact PR head from a clean laptop/Qube checkout, inspect failing shards if any, restore hosted Node/Swift CI, then execute the real Qubes qualification runner.
